proposal.utterance: Classify 'Abusus' (the right of abuse, in Roman-law property theory) in BFO terms.

entities.label: Abusus
entities.rationale: Abusus is the right (power) to alienate, consume, or destroy a thing — one of the three classical sticks of dominium (usus, fructus, abusus). As a type of legal right, it is a role borne by a property-holder: it is externally grounded in a legal system's recognition of ownership, not in any intrinsic physical property of the bearer or the thing. It is a kind (common noun), not a particular individual, so it is classed as a class. It is a sub-kind of LegalRight (which is already typed as BFO_0000023 Role / BFO_0000020 SDC). Modeling it as a Role rather than a Disposition is correct because its existence depends on the social-legal framework (external grounding), not on an internal causal power of the bearer.

relations.rationale: Abusus is a specific kind of legal right recognized in Roman-law property theory; LegalRight is already in the ontology as a subclass of BFO_0000023 (Role), making this the most parsimonious placement.

open_questions: Should Abusus also bear a relation to a class representing 'Dominium' (the full ownership bundle) as its bearer or whole? If so, we may need to mint a Dominium class and a mereological or dependency relation.
Should the other sticks — Usus (right of use) and Fructus (right to fruits) — be minted as sibling classes under LegalRight at the same time, to complete the Roman dominium triad?

Is Abusus being modeled purely in its Roman-law historical sense (a class of rights within Roman legal systems), or should it also cover modern civil-law analogues (e.g., French droit d'abusus under Art. 544 C.civ.)? This affects whether a single class suffices or whether role-sub-kinds per jurisdiction are needed.

The bearer of an Abusus role instance is presumably a legal person (dominus). Should we assert a domain restriction that Abusus inheres in (RO_0000052) instances of a LegalPerson class? That class is not yet in the ontology.

Abusus also implicates a correlative object — the thing (res) over which the right is held. Should we model this via an object-property linking Abusus to a class of owned things (Material entity or Site)?
proposal.rationale_summary: Abusus — the Roman-law right of abuse or alienation — is best typed as a class whose instances are Roles (BFO_0000023). A Role in BFO is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer and is externally grounded, meaning its existence depends on facts about the social-legal environment rather than any intrinsic physical disposition of the bearer. Abusus paradigmatically satisfies this: a dominus holds the Abusus role only because a legal system recognizes and constitutes that entitlement; the role inheres in the person, not the thing. The existing class LegalRight (already a subclass of BFO_0000023 and BFO_0000020) is the natural parent, as Abusus is one species of legal entitlement within the tripartite dominium bundle (usus, fructus, abusus). It is minted as a class rather than an individual because 'Abusus' denotes a kind of right that many owners can instantiate. No new BFO top-level category is required.
